content: The test image shows a close-up of soybean stems/petioles with irregular dark reddish-brown blotches/discoloration, particularly concentrated on the stem surface. There appear to be hairy stems with necrotic tissue at a node junction. Let me compare against top candidates.

**Analysis Summary:**

**Test image observations:**
- Close-up of soybean stems/petioles
- Irregular dark reddish-brown blotching/discoloration distributed along stem surfaces
- Plant is still green/alive with green pods visible (mid-late season)
- Necrotic tissue visible at a node junction
- No white cottony growth, no linear rows of black specks, no leaf symptoms

**Candidate comparison:**
- **Anthracnose**: "Irregularly shaped red to dark brown blotches on stems and petioles" — matches the irregular reddish-brown stem blotching pattern perfectly
- **Diaporthe**: Requires visible linear rows of black pycnidia — not present
- **Phytophthora**: Dark brown girdling lesion from taproot base upward — doesn't match this scattered irregular pattern
- **Charcoal Rot**: Requires gray/charcoal coloring with microsclerotia — not present
- **White Mold**: Requires white cottony mycelium/sclerotia — not present

The irregular reddish-brown to dark brown blotches on the stems and petioles of an otherwise green/actively podding plant are classic Anthracnose stem blight symptoms.
